**Proposed mechanism:** POLH variant (rs35366465) —DISRUPTS→ POLH (HGNC:9000); POLH (HGNC:9000) —DISRUPTS→ DNA repair (nucleotide excision repair) (GO:0006298); DNA repair (nucleotide excision repair) (GO:0006298) —LEADS_TO→ Xeroderma pigmentosum (HP:0000964); SPTN variant (rs143572900) —DISRUPTS→ SPTN (HGNC:11160); SPTN (HGNC:11160) —DISRUPTS→ DNA repair (homologous recombination, DNA damage checkpoint) (GO:0000724); SPTN (HGNC:11160) —DISRUPTS→ Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049); DNA repair (homologous recombination, DNA damage checkpoint) (GO:0000724) —LEADS_TO→ Progeroid features (HP:0003674); Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatocellular carcinoma predisposition (HP:0002671); DNA repair (nucleotide excision repair) (GO:0006298) —LEADS_TO→ Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049). Mutations in POLH (XPV) impair nucleotide excision repair, while mutations in SPRTN (progeroid syndrome) impair homologous recombination and DNA damage checkpoint pathways, and cell cycle regulation. Both DNA repair and cell cycle regulation are interconnected processes that, when disrupted, can lead to genomic instability and the characteristic phenotypes of each disease. The convergence occurs at the level of cell cycle regulation and DNA damage response pathways, which are critical for maintaining genomic integrity.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of mutations in POLH or SPRTN in individuals with the other disease's phenotype, without mutations in their typically associated genes, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, identification of specific genetic variants in POLH or SPRTN with high allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD populations would question their role as causative for rare Mendelian diseases. _(variant: rs35366465)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis in DNA repair and cell cycle regulation could lead to the development of targeted therapies that enhance DNA repair capacity or modulate cell cycle checkpoints, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
